segments.subgoal: Explain what IMU sensors are, their components, and how gyroscope data drives tracking while accelerometers and magnetometers aid drift detection.
Describe how calibration estimates a mathematical mapping from a cheap sensor's angular velocity readings to ideal values using sample comparisons and least-squares regression.
Explain how registration establishes the initial pose or orientation and alignment between real and virtual worlds, often using fiducial markers or computer vision.
Describe how integration computes the current orientation by adding successive calibrated angular velocity samples to the initial orientation from registration.
Explain how drift correction reduces estimation error by blending orientation estimates from multiple sensors using a gain parameter.
Summarize the main points of the lecture, including the four tracking stages, and indicate that specific sensing technologies will be covered next.
